results.title: r/Recruitment on Reddit: Has anyone actually had their LinkedIn account restricted for using automation tools?
results.snippet: I keep seeing recruiters using tools like Dripify, Expandi, Waalaxy and LinkedIn's crackdown seems to be getting more aggressive. Curious how widespread the actual account restriction problem is in practice, vs just a scare tactic to get you onto their paid products.

results.title: Why LinkedIn Automation Tools Get Your Account Banned (And What to Do Instead)
results.snippet: Policy changes. Tools your team used 18 months ago may now trigger instant restrictions after policy updates. LinkedIn's enforcement posture can shift at any time.

results.title: r/LeadGeneration on Reddit: Expandi / Dripify suddenly leading to Linkedin restrictions/warnings?
results.snippet: I've been using Dripify for years... Suprisingly I've never been flagged lol. I have used other tools like Salesflow, or duxsoup and even expandi and I've been flagged. But not like a crazy amount of times. ... Thanks for the data points! ... linkedin has been tightening the screws on all automation tools lately.....

results.title: What Happens When LinkedIn Bans Your Automation Tool? (2026)
results.snippet: Yes. LinkedIn's detection systems identify patterns created by automation extensions. Extensions used by tools like PhantomBuster and Dripify have been flagged this way.

results.title: LinkedIn Automation Safety 2026 - Valley
results.snippet: Northlight.ai's Q1 2026 analysis quantified this pattern: roughly 40% of accounts using non-compliant automation tools - explicitly naming HeyReach, Expandi, Dripify, and Waalaxy - received some form of restriction between January and March 2026.
